entries.en:
The young knight, charmed by the harpy's magic, had been
going to see his strange new lover at her nest every night.

The harpy's top half is a human woman's torso, with a giant
bird's legs and tail. His infatuation seems very strange, but
nothing makes him happier.

One night she opens her wings wide and he holds his lover,
burying his face in her bosom tenderly. He notices similarities
between her and his late belle, when the harpy's talons tear
into his back.

The only harpies ever seen have always been female, with a
woman's body wed to a bird's wings and talons. Some
speculate that they reproduce by mating with human men.

While they may appear beautiful, harpies are very violent and
cruel. Thus, not much research has been done on them... but
what of their chicks? Surely, a smaller, weaker subject would
be much less of a problem to deal with...

However, the researchers were wrong. The hungry chicks
devoured the researchers, and any thoughts of
communicating with them have been destroyed.

An advanced detachment of orc troops had been invading the
ruins, and were absentmindedly feeding on honey buzzard
eggs and chicks. This resulted in a marked decline of
Hydeland's honey buzzard population.

These large avians typically build their nests in caves and
ruins. They eat insects, reptiles, other birds, eggs, small
mammals, etc. Their favorite foods appear to be wasps, and
they will actively attack wasp nests in order to get at them.
This leads to their nicknames of "Wasp-Eaters" or "Bug
Buzzards".

With the orcs driven off, the wasp population will likely be
reined in once again.

The ancestors of dragons have come to light through ancient
Elician texts. These primogenitors adapted to the land and
sea and flourished, possessing all manner of shapes and skills.

Ancient magicians, in an attempt to take the great power of
the dragons for their own, tried to create a spell to control
and enslave these dragons. It is due to this arrogance that
Elicia was destroyed by the Ancient Dragon long ago.

Medusa is known throughout mythology as a beauty,
youngest of the Gorgon sisters. It is said that the goddess
Althena punished her for meeting men at the temple.

Her long and beautiful hair became snakes, her skin covered
in bronze-like scales, becoming a monster inside and out.
She hid in a remote area with her sisters who felt sorry for
her.

Medusa appeared at the temple again, enraged at the goddess,
but you put an end to her reign of terror by severing her
head. Shortly afterward, she turned to stone and crumbled.

Flying dragons are a direct result of human mages altering
the forms of dragons in ancient times. Because of this,
wyverns seem to have inherited memories that make them
view humans as ancestral enemies.

In captive conditions, only about 50% of wyvern eggs will
hatch. It is said that wyvern riders stay with their wyvern
mounts at all times, and after much training, they consume
some of each others' flesh as part of a ritual to complete a
blood-bond between the rider and beast.

Dark elves are antisocial by nature, even amongst
themselves, a trait which ultimately led to their demise at
the hands of other races.

Surviving dark elves were forced from their lands by other
elves, and mostly reside underground. Without a large central
population, it's unlikely that future generations will inherit and
carry on their customs.

However, some individual dark elves still wander the land,
using their magic to dominate violent beasts.

"You have the potential to be a beast-tamer, a very powerful
skill. Keep your bloodline going so you can spread this power
to your descendants," the dark elf tells you before departing,
never to be seen again.

If you hear the frightening cry of the banshee, superstitious
people claim this means your death is near.

Inside the sealed room where the treasure lay, bandits who
perished had become skeletons who would slaughter
any who set foot in the room.

Perhaps the disembodied woman's voice that was audible from
this room was in fact a banshee, crying to lament over those
who died, yet only drawing new victims to their graves.

You have successfully defeated the red dragon. Within the
dragon's treasure chambers, you discover the ring from
Meriad, the princess who gave her life to save her people.

For those who view your slaying of the dragon as an act of
the goddess' benedictions, this will no doubt galvanize their
own faith. However, the discovery of Meriad's ring also
energizes her followers.

Later, the Morneon Church declares Meriad's deeds as also
being the work of their goddesses. They canonize her as a
saint, and claim her as part of their own religion.

The Genie had grown frustrated that he was bound to remain
within the lamp for centuries, if not millennia, doing the
bidding of whomever held the lamp.

So, while he was out granting a wish, he wrote and submitted
a request in secret, plotting to have a third party take
possession of the lamp and grant the genie's wish: freedom
from the lamp's prison.

After having served the will of others for so long, the Genie
was glad to use his powers for himself for once. Not long
after, he had amassed a plethora of treasure and gained a
following of beautiful women from every corner of the globe.

Elliot Pid, the famed adventurer, sailed on his eponymous
ship to explore the world and seek glory. At some point he
must have lost the ship to pirates, who have used and
abused it ever since.

Now it is a ghost ship. The captain's logs tell epic tales of
dangers and treasure, and the last entries speak of fighting a
kraken, a giant sea monster encountered in unpioneered
waters.

Since then, the kraken has become famous, and its very
name is feared by sailors wherever they roam.

The greedy client tried to take all the treasure later, and was,
unsurprisingly, waylaid and killed by bandits.

His younger brother brought the body home for burial. The
bandits came after him too, but one of their slaves, a
stunning and cunning woman, had secretly replaced the wine
in the 40 vases the bandits were going to hide inside with oil,
and then burned them all to death.

The brother was so thankful for the slave's actions that he
married her to his own son. He then claimed the bandits'
treasure and shared it with all the people of his village.
One could say that they made out like bandits.

The three men followed you to see if you would emerge
victorious over the kraken, as Anna Bonnie did. However,
before reaching the kraken, you battled monster bats,
skeletons, armored demi-beasts, and the like. These battles
were so terrifying that all three men fled in fear.

And so, none witnessed your battle with the kraken, and
none saw you perform a deed which rivaled the great
Anna Bonnie's legendary exploits.

To this day, the three men still drink to and speak of Anna
Bonnie with much admiration, and her name sparks hopes and
desires in the hearts of sailors.

While what you discovered was still a baby, the sea serpent
looks exactly like the wall paintings.

If the stories in ancient texts are true, this serpentling
should grow even larger than a red dragon.

This living fossil is an ancient amphibian who shares a
common ancestor with the dragons who ruled the world in
ancient times. Thus, their strength and power are notable,
though the texts say that their intelligence was beastly.

The seven boys and seven girls who were to be sacrificed
to the minotaur had been saved. One of the boys had
secretly been unraveling a ball of string he carried with him
into the labyrinth so they would be able to follow the thread
back out.

The minotaur, who has the head of a cow and the body of a
human, is said to be an apostle of a heretic religion that
fanatic orcs follow. They treated it kindly at first, but later
trapped it deep underground after tiring of its violent nature.

The goblins were secretly sharpening their fangs against
their own allies, the orcs, who had taken control of Bilbaron
Fortress. The goblins' long-term goal was to build a flying
fortress, the Sky Terror.

Recovered designs show it to be the size of a giant whale,
able to hold over 100 goblins. It boasts twenty massive
cannons, and can move at such a speed that it would be able
to cross the length of Hydeland in one night. The amount of
skycrime the goblins could commit with it is unfathomable.

Thanks to your efforts, their dreams were crushed before
they could come to fruition. You likely saved the entire
kingdom.

Javleen's handkerchief was returned to the woman intact,
thus honoring the last promise he made.

An oft-decorated knight commander, Javleen is a hero who,
with his prized horse and trusty weapon, rode out into the
front lines with his knights and won one hundred battles
against the orc army.

He died in battle at Gargoyle Gate, but his work in boosting
the morale of Hydeland's army will be spoken of in legends
for generations to come.

Dwarven crafters have incredible technical skills that are
passed down through generations. Human engineers have
given the world great scientific innovations, and the dark
elves, though few in number, have a wealth of unique skills
and knowledge.

Bilbaron Fortress and its impregnable gate were created with
the combined efforts and abilities of many races. One of
those contributing architects tells you, without hesitation, to
destroy the gate, for they will band together once again to
build something even stronger and greater to replace it.

Floating cities, twisted plants, insects the likes of which
have never been seen... The researchers who successfully
peered into the souls of gazers saw fantastical scenery that
was quite unlike the reality they knew.

The researchers began furiously detailing the sights of the
netherworld they had witnessed. However, they were not
well received by the general public.

Apparently, society did not appreciate the subject matter and
were worried that the researchers' depictions of the
netherworld would only stoke certain peoples' desires to
visit it.

When you return with the amethysts, you learn that the
requester has been captured by the guards.

She turned out not to be a sculptor, but a heretic magician
who specialized in research concerning the undead...
She has a long list of prior grave robbery convictions to 
her name.

Pure amethysts trap magic extremely well and are used as
mediums for fortune tellers and witches.

The requester was trying to inject a spell into the amethysts
and embed them in the flesh of corpses to create high
functioning undead.

In an attempt to harness golem might, the heathen magicians
of Morneon have been experimenting with golemetry. Tired
of mere Wood Golems, they moved on to trying to control
the ambulating and benevolent wise old tree, Torent.

The forest, formerly beautifully maintained by the elves,
became a dangerous place after the affliction of the miasma
grew stronger.

Outlaws and strange mages now use the forest as hideouts,
attacking adventurers and patrol squads. The elves grieved
and shook with anger.

A number of years ago, when a group of knights pursuing a
holy relic stepped into a cave, the ones that fled reported
that their retinue were viciously waylaid by a rabbit there.
Rumors of this foul, terrifying lagomorph spread.

Today, many bloodthirsty knights in the neighboring country
of Bolga, in an attempt to make a name for themselves, go
to challenge the killer rabbit. They only manage to increase
its body count.

The duplicitous duke made this request in an attempt to
generate a similar phenomenon in our kingdom. However, as
long as a true hero like you calls Hydeland home, such
attempts at trickery will be in vain.

For a moment, you saw the shadow of an otherworldly being
on the bottom of the lake. 

There are rumors of a human man who fell in love with
Scylla, a beautiful mermaid. Because they lived in different
worlds, the man asked a witch to cast a spell so that he
could be with his love.

However, the witch took a liking to this man, and instead
cast a spell on both of them to destroy her mermaid rival.
The beautiful mermaid was transmogrified into a monster,
the man lost his memory, and the witch wooed Scylla's lover.

The mermaid still waits at the bottom of the lake for the day
she encounters the two again.

The spells used to create golems are ancient, and the
thought process behind creating them is completely different
from the present day schools of magic. Golem magic is
beyond the mastery of even the researchers who are on the
cutting edge of magical experimentation.

It is said that not many who can wield that kind of magic
exist in this era, but over a century ago, there was one
young genius runic mage that kept their talents out of the
public eye.

The young Lisley could simultaneously control many golems
with her raw magical talent. The notes say that she would
play with them as if they were dolls.

You return, having survived the sharp fangs and fire of the
hellhounds. The man who hired you seems pleased with the
results.

Hellhounds are feared as creatures of evil, but the man
asserts that this is mere superstition. He says that canines
and humans have been friends since before the dawn of
history.

In an unsurprising turn of events, the man who so fondly
dreamed of holding a young hellpup in his arms went missing
soon after and was never heard from again.

In the days of mythology, the angels who were tasked with
overseeing humanity gave them knowledge and magic.
Humans immediately began using these gifts to fight each
other, and God lamented the devastation. He imprisoned
the angels responsible. 

Thus humans began calling these fallen angels demons.
These fallen angels, cast out of the heavens and feeling
betrayed by humans, embraced their new evil typecasting. 

Thanks to your efforts, the man is freed from the contract
he signed with the demons, and joins a monastery. One has
to wonder if the demons' attitudes towards humanity are
not justified...

The Morneon splinter sect known as the "Hell Evangelists"
has attracted many followers who were seeking spirituality
and enlightenment.

They had no sociopolitical agenda, and were only seeking to
further an objective understanding of black magic. However,
there have been some recent schisms within the sect. The
more radical faction does not seem to care for morals or
common decency.

Even if their interests and the kingdom's were aligned,
working with this faction would not benefit Hydeland in the
long run. As such, the kingdom has decided to cut ties to this
cult.

Perhaps the monk's blind faith worked; destroying the statue
of the false god completely removed the temptations from
the monk's dreams.

Sometimes, those who discipline themselves the hardest are
ones who are the most likely to break. The demons who
wield dominion over lust can find the smallest crack in a
person's psyche to tempt them down the path of
destruction.

It is likely that the monk will never truly be free from this
problem, and the incubi's promises of otherwordly parties and
pleasures may one day prove too much for him to resist.

The researchers repeatedly experimented on the bodily fluid
samples you brought back, and created a giant worm. As
aberrations of nature created in a research lab are wont to
do, this worm later destroyed the lab and escaped, and began
breeding unchecked in the nearby forest.

This causes no end of trouble for local residents, although
some adventurers passing through the area report that the
worms do serve as a convenient source of protein.

Doom Beetles, which are influenced by strong magic while
still in cocoons, may sometimes emerge with a giant horn.
The magician Wallace seems to have made a connection
between the magic and the beetles' evolution, and had been
working to speed up their mutation process.

Surprisingly, Rickey is a successful example of Wallace's
experiments. Rickey squeaks enthusiastically and says that
he will work hard to complete his master's research.

The fungi incubation experiment was held in an
environment protected from the effects of magic by
tripling the normal amount of sacred barriers.

The fungi did not grow like the myconids, but neither did
they grow to be poisonous. At the same time, it was
discovered that the taste of the non-poisonous fungi is
quite terrible.

While these results disappointed the gourmands, the
researchers don't seem to be deterred. They will continue
their fungus research regardless.

The Goddess gave birth to many creatures and deities,
including the race of giants known as the cyclopes. Morneon
seemed to be under the assumption that by releasing the
myopia of cyclopes - her creations - they would gain her
favor and she would give birth to a great new monster that
they could control.

However, they had no actual way to possibly communicate
with either the Goddess or the giants. Their messenger was
trampled and killed the instant he opened the cell door.

On a whim, the witch Lima Ray helped the goblins being
persecuted by the elves and ended the elf nuisance for
them. After that, the goblins worshipped her as a living god.

Lima Ray's powerful magic worked in tandem with the goblins
who served as her transportation, and they went around the
world causing all kinds of mayhem. 

The goblins would love to return to those glory days. Thus,
they have been conspiring to bring her back from the dead
with a spell she had taught them. However, without Lima
Ray, it's a simple matter to crush their ambitions. You easily
staved off her attempted resurrection.

The hunter appears before you after you have finished off
the last of the vampires. He is clad in black armor and has a
comely face. The request he received was to expose the
partnership between the local priest and the vampires. The
priest had become enamored with the vampires, and instead
of trying to purge the world of their evil, he actually created
a cursed seal to invite them to the village.

The hunter leaves silently before the sun rises. There is
nothing more for you to do. The priest will be judged by the
villagers accordingly.

Rumor holds that some of the kidnapped girls became
vampires and adapted to their new lifestyle. They were freed
from their lives of poverty and grew to become powerful
leaders of their vampire clan. The wealth and power of the
clans grew, and the vampire leaders infiltrated noble society.

Desiccated beautiful flowers have a certain charm to some,
and the undead's reach spread throughout high society. Not
many in the upper classes have even realized the influence
of the vampires has spread so far.

The death of the landlord's family was due to an epidemic.
Carried by rats and flies, it spread like wildfire - it was not
uncommon for an entire village to be devastated overnight.

The landlord's family died at their final rave. This gala was
held during the height of the outbreak, and in their frenzied
terror the party-goers began dancing madly, day and night,
some even dying on their feet.

Even today, the skeletons dance side by side with humans.
Death comes to all, regardless of class or wealth.

Legends claim that the death god first appeared to humans
when some of the deities granted the powers of
resurrection to some people, and souls that were marked
for death weren't making the journey to the afterlife.

The father laments that his resurrected daughter took the
hand of a young man and eloped. The anti-resurrection
league firmly believes that souls should be sent naturally to
heaven, even if this means losing their own children.

Perhaps in their eyes, the terrifying death gods look like
beautiful angels leading souls to heaven.

The unusually large wight rules over the other skeletal
swordsmen. He watches over the colosseum.

When he was alive, he was too big to be a knight, but could
only release his aggressive impulses by fighting. Even after
death, he could not stop, and so he led other skeletons with
similar unending drives to join together for a neverending
battle.

The hero Roland admires these warriors, and has excitedly
requested that he be buried there when he dies himself.

When you touch the temples of the leader of the
underground organization, you feel his memories flooding
through your fingertips.

The young man, once burning with dreams and ideals,
blossomed in his talent for black magic and even became a
teacher. However, those days ended, and his hope turned
to despair. When he was falsely blamed for spreading a raging
epidemic, his girlfriend and his family were all executed. 

Since then, his path has become twisted. He sold his soul
to the devil in an attempt to destroy this crazy kingdom
where evil is passed off as justice.

The "correct" way for a dragon worshipper to live his life is
to admire the great beasts' bodies and train himself to be
stronger, but this man wanted more: he wanted to become
one. He researched a taboo art used to fuse dragons and
humans together.

Fusion of humans and creatures to create hybrid lifeforms
is wrong on a fundamental level. This work will only create
cursed beings, and all of his research materials were burned.

A dancing doll was discovered behind the hidden door in
Henritta's room.

The mechanics of the automatic doll's movements were
created by applying golem magic to machinery, which comes
as a disappointment to the requester.

Henritta had not been trying to replicate the human body,
nor create artificial power; she had sought the smaller
wonder of love. The automatic doll will dance forever, as if
seeking to protect the dreams of her deceased master.

"If a new body can be created to house it, a soul can be
resurrected. If a human soul can be preserved repeatedly,
then it can live forever." Or so the man claimed.

The reality of the situation is that a homunculus can only
live within the container it was created in; if it leaves, the
body collapses and it dies instantly. The church
excommunicated the man, burned his research, and
explicitly forbade any further research on homunculi.

The spinning wheel you found in the tower belonged to
Arachne, the great weaver. In ancient times long past, the
poor girl's bottom half was turned into that of a spider to
punish her for her conceit.

Arachne later had a change of heart, and lived quietly in a
remote area, making beautiful carpets from her own silken
thread. Despite her newfound humility, the beauty and magic
of her carpets only angered the gods even further.

When owlbears were declared to be a menace, owlbear
hunting became popular, and their numbers dropped sharply
at the hands of adventurers and hunters.

Once their coats became sought after amongst the nobles,
they were hunted even more intensely, and they quickly
became an endangered species.

Some of the wise scholars point out that it is quite
hypocritical that it was humans who brought these creatures
into the world, and now humans are trying to slaughter them.

Your copious amount of fish destruction was overshadowed
by the sudden appearance of a mysterious fisherman. He
apparently went about slaughtering the fish with an amazing
spearing display.

Ancient myths state that the killer fish committed the sin of
gluttony and were duly punished by the sea god. Whenever
the sea god isn't nearby, they take advantage of the
opportunity and eat everything in the water.

The mysterious fisherman's identity is unknown, but his
shell horn leads people to speculate that he is a form of
the sea god.

The guildmaster Samuel welcomes you back after defeating
the swordsmen. When he was a young knight, he was
captured by the Bolgan Kingdom in a battle along the
northern border. The prisoners were forced to fight in
mortal gladiatorial combat.

Samuel won battle after battle, winning the favor of the
crowd. Another fighter became popular as well, and even
renounced his Hydeland citizenship to live in Bolga. Now,
as an old soldier, he commands the Bolgan knights invading
Hydeland.

Samuel feels a premonition that he will have to stand on the
battlefield again to face his former rival.

The Amazons of the south are an all-female tribe who fight
with great ferocity.

In order to protect their independence, they have created
an isolated society and constantly battle enemy nations.
In this culture, warriors are highly valued, and becoming a
warrior requires fierce trials and rituals.

Completing the trial of taking 50 orcs' heads has earned
you the trust of the Amazons, and status equal to that of
a warrior. Their efforts have slowed the progress of the
invading orc army.

The cape created by the witch Morgan Lisley is a one-of-a-
kind item made by enchanting each thread as she wove it. It
is an ultimate example of exquisite and delicate detail.

While it is light, it is amazingly resilient. Adventurers began
to fight for possession of this rare item.

Morgan was sent mountains of spider webs, but she never
made another such cape. Indeed, she was sick of all the
commotion over the first one.

You were awarded the title of Saint March Rosa in
recognition of your exemplary efforts.

The original March Rosa healed many illnesses with medical
care and medicine. This was different from the unscientific
remedies the priests were prescribing, and thus surprised
the church and made them fearful. 

March Rosa's medical skills only grew, and eventually, he
made the dead come back to life using Medusa's blood which
he allegedly got from a goddess. He continued healing until
he was felled by a lightning bolt.

The fairies trapped in the cage were dreaming. They come
from the Great Forest, their home and the origin of the fairy
race. It was where the fairy king used to rule, a paradise
where all fairies could freely dance and sing.

On Walpurgis Night, demons, humans, and fairies could all
celebrate together. If it is a dream, then everyone should be
able to take part regardless of species. The fairies wish and
hope that this night will come.

Among historians, there is a lot of doubt about what you truly
accomplished, likely because you never spoke of it yourself.

Only when Hydeland's official records of the hero who
defeated the ancient dragon were published did your deeds
come to light. Those records chronicle your deeds in many
lands. At the end of each, you return to Hydeland and drink
at the Dragon's Haven Inn.

The tales patrons claim you told, of the land in the sky, or
the one ring, become oral tradition passed on for generations.
The last mention of your name says you ventured far into
the sea in your seventies, but even after a half century,
some still wait...

You suddenly remember the moment you left the village.

You had just been acknowledged as a mature warrior. Long
ago, in the wildlands, a carriage was waylaid by orcs. Only an
infant survived - you. The amazons raised you as their own.

You came to Hydeland to discover your roots, but you had
given up by the time the Dragon's Crown incident occurred.
While the citizens grant you a hero's welcome, an elderly
noble couple look at you in stunned surprise.

They will soon realize that you have the same eyes as their
son, who died years ago in a remote land...

The dwarves had once built a great kingdom underground.
Now, the few surviving dwarves lived banded together in
small villages. They were nearly exterminated by the ancient
dragon, and the underground kingdom became his.

The dwarves dub you the noble avenger and convey heroic
status upon you. Your words are given incredible weight.
Dwarves drink with you and dream of a great and powerful
nation led by the noble avenger.

Their hopes are rightly placed, as you will eventually lead
them to glory, your name echoing throughout the halls of
time.

The elves' kingdom is deep in a forest where humans never
tread. Elves don't trust outsiders. Most have never seen a
human. You, however, dreamt of adventure and leaving the
forest. That made you a bit of a social outcast.

You return to the forest after a long hiatus, worried about
how you would be treated now that you have human and
dwarf friends. To your surprise, you were treated well in all
the land.

The elf king even granted you the title of Crown Regent.
He's relieved because elves had foretold of the ancient
dragon's revival, but laws dictated the king must fight it.

You became quite a hit with the nobles. Perhaps they
thought an alluring, powerful sorceress could grant their
every desire.

Enticed by the glamorous life you'd always dreamed of, you
do prophecies and palm readings to enjoy life in high society.
People criticized you for trading in your old life for the finer
things, but that wasn't true. You were working for the
kingdom.

Your prophecies were clever distractions from the nobles'
worries, avarice, and ambitions. You placated all their unrest. 
But this mundane life bores you. You long for ale from the
Dragon's Haven Inn. It isn't luxury you crave, but adventure...

An arrogant young magician was attempting to save his
sister's life by tinkering with immortality spells beyond
his ken.

Worry became elation as you saw your sister drift into a
deep sleep, obviously free of the pain that plagued her
every moment. Sadly, your joy was fleeting.

She neither breathed nor woke again. Your spell left her in
limbo; neither alive nor dead. Your journey was a quest to
save her from your foolish actions. You traveled the world
before ending up at Hydeland.

Now, you return as a great magician to fix your error.
You distilled the ancient dragon blood to create the elixir...

The heavens and earth were created, followed by a
tumultuous period where deities, giants, and dragons lived
together, but after the humans became rulers of the world,
the balance was kept by three guardian deities; the goddess
Jula, deity of trees and hunting, the goddess Vernas, deity of
love and harvest, and the goddess Althena, deity of battles
and mercy.

These goddesses are said to have nobly sacrificed their
powers to seal the ancient dragon in the Illusionary Land
in order to save the world.
